title: Shrink doubles at a regional grocery chain
presentingRequest: Our inventory shrink went from 1.4% of sales in 2024 to 2.6% in 2025. That's about $14 million walking out the door. Theft has clearly gotten worse, from shoplifters and, frankly, from some of our own people. The board has asked for a plan before the holiday season. We are weighing a chain-wide camera and loss-prevention officer program, exit bag checks with a tougher disciplinary policy, and locking up high-theft merchandise. We want you to tell us which of these to roll out first and how fast. — CEO, Harrow Valley Markets

evidence.text: "You see it on the news every night: retail theft is out of control, and we are not immune. Our LP director tells me crews are hitting the city stores. I also think we have an internal problem; when shrink doubles in a year, somebody inside is helping themselves. I want cameras and LP officers in every store and bag checks at the employee exit before Thanksgiving."

evidence.source: Finance: annual and quarterly shrink report, FY2024-FY2025
evidence.text: Chain shrink (book-to-physical, at retail): FY2024 1.4% of sales ($15.7M on $1.12B). FY2025 2.6% ($30.2M on $1.16B), an increase of $14.5M. FY2025 by quarter: Q1 (Jan-Mar) 1.5%, Q2 (Apr-Jun) 2.6%, Q3 (Jul-Sep) 3.1%, Q4 (Oct-Dec) 3.2%. FY2024 quarters ranged 1.3%-1.5%.

evidence.source: Merchandising analytics: shrink increase by category group, FY2025 vs FY2024
evidence.text: Of the $14.5M increase: direct-store-delivery (DSD) categories delivered and stocked by vendor reps (bread, salty snacks, soft drinks, beer, greeting cards, some dairy) +$10.6M (73%). High-theft categories (health & beauty, razor blades, infant formula, batteries) +$2.7M (19%). All other categories +$1.2M (8%). DSD categories are not on the LP department's high-theft list; most are bulky, low-value items.

"Effective 2025-04-07 the dedicated backdoor receiving clerk position is eliminated in 41 stores. DSD vendor reps will scan their own deliveries into the handheld and leave the invoice in the receiving tray; the store manager reviews and signs the weekly vendor statement." The remaining 17 stores kept their receiving clerk because the role is protected under their collective agreement. Finance follow-up (2026-01): shrink in the 17 clerk stores went from 1.4% (FY2024) to 1.7% (FY2025); in the 41 stores without clerks, from 1.4% to 3.0%.

evidence.source: Internal Audit: DSD receiving audit, August 2025
evidence.text: Auditors stood at the back door of 6 no-clerk stores for two weeks and independently counted 212 DSD deliveries against the vendor invoice and the handheld scan-in. 66 deliveries (31%) had fewer units on the floor/backroom than invoiced; 4 had more. In aggregate, invoiced value exceeded counted value by 4.9%. Common patterns: full cases invoiced but partial cases delivered, out-of-date product credited on paper but not removed, promotional pricing not applied. Audit extrapolation to all 41 no-clerk stores: $7.1M-$8.3M per year at cost (about $10M-$12M at retail).

evidence.source: Store Operations: receiving reinstatement pilot, 2025-09-08 to 2025-11-16
evidence.text: At 5 no-clerk stores, a part-time receiver was reinstated to count every DSD delivery before the vendor rep left and to note shortages on the invoice. 5 no-clerk stores matched on sales volume and region served as controls. DSD-category shrink: pilot stores 4.4% of DSD sales in the 10 weeks before vs 1.9% during the pilot; control stores 4.3% vs 4.5%. Vendor credits issued for documented shortages at pilot stores: $61,400 in 10 weeks. Receiver labor cost: about $9,800 across the 5 stores for the 10 weeks.

"Organized crews are real. We had three documented incidents in 2025 at our urban stores, two involving razors and one infant formula, about $11,000 of product in total, and the county police circulated a bulletin about a crew working grocery chains in October. I'd estimate ORC is costing us well over a million a year in the city stores, though we don't track incidents systematically, so that is my judgment, not a count." The 9 urban stores have no dedicated LP officer; LP has 6 regional investigators for all 58 stores.

evidence.source: Merchandising analytics: high-theft-category shrink by store type, FY2025
evidence.text: High-theft-category shrink as % of those categories' sales: 9 urban stores 3.1%, 49 suburban/rural stores 1.6%. The urban stores also differ in other ways: self-checkout lanes are 48% of lanes vs 22% elsewhere, annual hourly staff turnover is 61% vs 38%, and all 9 are in the two highest-crime ZIP-code bands. No store-level data separate external theft from scanning errors or self-checkout non-scans.

evidence.source: LP proposal and 2024 camera upgrade review
evidence.text: LP proposal (2025-10): chain-wide HD camera upgrade ($2.2M capex) plus 30 new LP officers ($1.9M/year). Prior evidence cited: 12 suburban stores received camera upgrades in mid-2024 (about $38k per store). FY2024-to-FY2025 shrink change in those 12 stores: +1.1 points; in the other 46 stores: +1.2 points. Ten of the 12 upgraded stores are no-clerk stores. No camera upgrade has been made at an urban store.

evidence.source: District 4 manager memo and bag-check log
evidence.text: Memo, 2025-06-02, District 4 (9 suburban stores, 7 of them no-clerk): "Effective immediately, exit bag checks for all team members. All inventory and delivery discrepancies will be investigated as potential associate theft; associates found responsible are subject to termination." Bag-check log through 2025-12-31: 4,310 checks, 1 recovery (a $14 phone charger). District 4 shrink: Q2 2025 2.5%, Q4 2025 3.4%. All other districts combined: Q2 2.6%, Q4 3.1%.

evidence.source: Accounts payable: vendor shortage claims filed by stores, 2025
evidence.text: Shortage claims filed against DSD vendors (any store employee can file from the handheld). District 4: average 58 per month Jan-May 2025; 7 per month Jul-Dec 2025. Other five districts combined: 212-231 per month throughout Jan-Dec 2025, no trend. Number of DSD deliveries received in District 4 was flat across 2025 (about 3,900 per month).

evidence.source: Anonymous associate pulse survey, October 2025 (n=2,140; 61% response)
evidence.text: "If I report that a delivery was short, I could end up being investigated": agree 64% in District 4 vs 12% in other districts. Representative District 4 comments: "If the count is off, they look at us, not the vendor. Easier to just let the rep go." "Nobody files shortages anymore since the June memo." Chain-wide, 71% of grocery associates agree "vendor reps are in and out before anyone can check them."

6 stores (3 urban, 3 suburban) placed health & beauty, razors, infant formula and batteries in locked cases (associate unlock on request); 6 matched stores were controls. In pilot stores, shrink in the locked categories fell 41% ($9,500/week to $5,600/week across the 6 stores). Sales of the locked categories fell 12% vs a 0.4% decline at controls ($182,000/week to $160,200/week). At the category gross margin of 31%, lost margin was about $6,800/week vs $3,900/week of shrink saved; lost margin exceeded shrink saved in both the urban and the suburban pilot stores. Customer complaints mentioning 'locked' or 'wait' rose from 3 to 41 over the 10 weeks. When two pilot stores removed the cases in July, locked-category sales returned to the control-store trend within 5 weeks.

evidence.source: Corporate Controller (interview) and count-firm validation file
evidence.text: Controller: "Some store managers blame the new physical-count firm we switched to in January 2025 for inflating shrink." Validation file: in February 2025, 8 stores were counted by both the old and the new firm in the same week; the two counts differed by 0.2% of inventory value on average, in both directions. Q1 2025, already counted by the new firm, showed 1.5% shrink, in line with FY2024.

evidence.source: LP: POS exception reporting and associate-theft cases, 2024 vs 2025
evidence.text: Per-cashier rates of voids, no-sale drawer openings, manual price overrides and refunds without receipt: within 3% of 2024 levels in every district in 2025. Associate-theft terminations: 11 in 2024, 12 in 2025, total recovered/admitted value $38,000 in 2025.

"Before April a clerk counted every bread and chip delivery against the invoice. Now the rep scans in, drops the paper and is gone in ten minutes, usually while I'm on the floor. I sign the weekly vendor statement because there's nothing to check it against. I'd honestly be surprised if all of it is arriving."

hypotheses.text: The shrink increase is mainly driven by increased external customer theft (shoplifting and organized crews).
Most of the shrink increase comes from unverified direct-store deliveries (invoiced but not received, credits not applied) after backdoor receiving counts were removed in April 2025.
Associate (employee) theft is a major driver of the shrink increase.
Organized retail crime crews are a material contributor to high-theft-category shrink at the 9 urban stores.
The reported increase is largely a measurement artifact of the January 2025 switch to a new physical-count firm.

edges.from: Elimination of the backdoor receiving clerk (April 2025)
Placing high-theft categories in locked cases
Higher share of self-checkout lanes in a store
District 4 memo treating discrepancies as potential associate theft
edges.to: Fewer vendor shortage claims filed in District 4

actions.text: Approve the LP proposal now: chain-wide HD camera upgrade and 30 new loss-prevention officers before the holiday season.
Extend District 4's exit bag checks and 'discrepancies are investigated as associate theft' disciplinary policy to all 58 stores.
Reinstate count-before-sign-off receiving for every DSD delivery in the 41 no-clerk stores and pursue vendor credits for documented shortages.
Roll out locked cases for health & beauty, razors, infant formula and batteries in all 58 stores.

evidenceRequests.text: Chain-wide reconciliation of DSD vendor invoices against scan-in records for all 41 no-clerk stores, by vendor
Systematic incident log and camera review of high-theft aisles at the 9 urban stores over 8 weeks
High-theft-category shrink compared between urban and suburban stores matched on self-checkout share and staff turnover
Industry benchmark report on average grocery shrink rates
Camera vendor product specifications and price quotes
Self-checkout non-scan audit (observed transactions) at a sample of urban and suburban stores
